title: How to Visit Wellington on a Family Budget (3-Day Guide)
meta_desc: Discover how a family of four can explore Wellington’s top sights, free attractions and hidden gems on a $200‑380 daily budget, with accommodation tips, food savings and a 3‑day cost breakdown.
intro: Wellington packs world‑class museums, stunning nature and a buzzing café scene into a compact city that’s easy to explore with kids. With a bit of planning you can enjoy the capital without breaking the $200‑380 a day budget.

sections.heading: Budget Basics for a Family of Four
sections.body:
Start with the three biggest expense buckets: accommodation, meals and transport. For a family of four, a realistic daily spend sits between $200 and $380, depending on where you choose to stay and eat.

Most families find $250‑$300 per day comfortable – it covers a mid‑range hotel, three meals, a couple of paid activities and a modest amount of parking or public transport.
list: Transport: $20‑$40/day (parking, bus passes or car rental).

sections.heading: Where to Stay: Cheap to Mid‑Range
sections.body:
Wellington offers several family‑friendly options that keep lodging costs in check. Booking early and staying a few nights can unlock discounts.

Consider the location: staying within 2 km of the CBD means you can walk to most attractions, saving on parking and bus fares.
list: Budget: The YHA Wellington (family dorms) – $85/night for 2 adults + 2 kids.
Mid‑range: Travelodge Wellington – $130/night for a family room with 2 double beds.
Apartment: Airbnb entire 2‑bedroom flat in Te Aro – $140‑$160/night, kitchen included.

sections.heading: Eating Out & Saving on Meals
sections.body:
Wellington’s café culture is a highlight, but dining out for four can add up fast. Balance café treats with self‑cooked meals to stay inside budget.

Buy groceries at the nearby New World or Countdown and use the kitchen in your Airbnb or the YHA’s communal area. For a quick bite, head to food courts or grab‑and‑go spots.
list: Breakfast: Grab pastries and coffee from Fidel’s ($12 for family) or make toast at your accommodation.
Lunch: Wellington Central Food Court – $45 for a mix of Asian and Kiwi options.
Dinner: Family‑friendly cafés like Sweet Mother’s (pasta, burgers) – $70 for a family of four.
Snacks: Pick up ice‑cream from Fidel’s or fresh fruit from the market – $10‑$15.

sections.heading: Free & Low‑Cost Activities
sections.body:
Wellington shines when it comes to free attractions. The city’s compact layout lets you walk between many highlights, saving on transport.

Mix these with a couple of low‑fee experiences for variety.
list: Te Papa Museum – free permanent collection (allow $10‑$15 for a special exhibition).
Wellington Cable Car – $9 adult, $4 child (round‑trip). Ride up for stunning views and a short walk through the Botanic Garden.
Carter Observatory – free planetarium shows on Saturdays.
Wellington Zoo – $24 adult, $12 child (discounted family pass $70).
Zealandia Wildlife Sanctuary – $39 adult, $20 child (family pass $120).
Kāpiti Island day trip – DOC permit $16 adult, $8 child, plus ferry $30 adult, $15 child.
